title: ISO adopts Paris Statement to strengthen global action on climate adaptation and resilience
editorial_brief: At the ISO Annual Meeting in Paris in early October 2026, ISO members endorsed a statement placing greater emphasis on adaptation to climate impacts and resilience of natural systems. The event was hosted by France's standards body, AFNOR. The decision concerns the direction of standards cooperation: standards can help organisations anticipate environmental risks and coordinate practical responses. It connects adaptation with wider issues including natural resources and the reliability of essential systems. This is an account of a policy commitment by the standards community, not an announcement that a new technical standard has been published.

title: ISO and UNDP launch world's first International Standard to advance action on the Sustainable Development Goals
editorial_brief: On 28 September 2026, ISO and the United Nations Development Programme launched ISO/UNDP 53001, a management system standard concerned with how organisations contribute to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Its intended users include businesses and public or non-profit institutions. The approach places sustainability objectives within management processes, rather than treating them solely as public commitments. Organisations can connect priorities to governance, assign responsibilities, examine results and improve over time. The publication was announced during ISO's Annual Meeting in Paris. The release concerns a published management system standard, not just a proposal for future work.

title: Road vehicles committee wins ISO's top award
editorial_brief: In September 2026, ISO recognised the international standards committee for road vehicles, ISO/TC 22, with its highest committee award. The recognition acknowledges a long-running programme of standards development across the automotive sector. Vehicle technology now incorporates more software, connectivity and data, while manufacturers also face new environmental challenges. The committee's standards work matters across these changing areas because vehicle manufacturers, suppliers and regulators depend on common technical approaches. This news item reports an award for a technical committee, not the publication of a particular new standard.

title: ISO Annual Meeting 2026 in Paris to tackle trust, AI and global resilience
editorial_brief: ISO announced that its 2026 Annual Meeting would be held in Paris from 28 September to 2 October, with AFNOR serving as host. The programme brought standards experts together with other public and private sector participants to discuss trust in changing economic and technical circumstances. Topics included artificial intelligence, international cooperation and resilience. The meeting was designed as a forum to exchange perspectives about how international standards support shared expectations across borders. An event announcement is different from an official decision or the publication of a technical standard; any specific outcomes should be checked separately.

title: ISO launches update to world's most widely used quality management standard for a new era of business
editorial_brief: ISO published the 2026 edition of ISO 9001, its quality management requirements standard, on 16 September 2026. The revised publication continues to address how organisations manage quality and meet customer requirements. ISO describes it as an update intended to remain useful as business operations, supply chains and technologies evolve. Organisations working with the earlier edition may wish to examine the new requirements and any applicable certification transition arrangements. This is a new edition of an existing standard rather than the launch of an unrelated framework. The editorial note does not describe clause-by-clause changes; users should consult authorised standard documents for that level of detail.

title: World-first International Standard launched as demand grows for better workplace support during menstruation and menopause
editorial_brief: ISO introduced ISO 45010 in September 2026 as workplace guidance about menstruation and menopause. It is aimed at employers and professionals responsible for people management and occupational health. The subject is how working conditions, organisational practices and support arrangements can better accommodate employees who encounter related health or wellbeing needs. The guidance sits alongside the wider ISO 45000 occupational health and safety family. Unlike an external medical assessment, the standard addresses the workplace environment and organisational response. The news concerns the availability of guidance, not an obligation applicable automatically to every employer.

title: Global public-private collaboration makes digital identity standards freely accessible worldwide
editorial_brief: A collaboration involving ISO, IEC, DIN and the OpenWallet Foundation was announced on 1 September 2026 to widen access to important digital credential standards. The arrangements concern the ISO/IEC 18013 and 23220 families, relevant to mobile driving licences and related credentials. Rather than reporting a new identity standard, the announcement addresses how implementers can obtain selected existing standards. The model relies on sponsorship to support free access while recognising that the documents remain subject to copyright. The practical significance is potentially wider use of common technical approaches in digital identity solutions.

title: ISO 14001:2026 published - raising the bar for environmental performance
editorial_brief: ISO released a revised edition of ISO 14001 on 15 April 2026. This standard describes requirements and supporting guidance for an environmental management system. The updated edition is intended to help organisations manage environmental responsibilities and assess progress through structured management processes. It is particularly relevant to firms reviewing their existing environmental management arrangements, assurance activities or supply-chain expectations. The announcement concerns the latest edition of an established management system standard. This editorial overview does not replace the official requirements or explain individual clauses, which need to be checked against a licensed copy of the standard.

title: Preparing for the unexpected: How ISO 22372 strengthens infrastructure resilience
editorial_brief: ISO highlighted ISO 22372:2025 in November 2025 as a standard relevant to the resilience of infrastructure and services. The underlying concern is that disruptions from natural hazards and other shocks can affect interconnected assets and the communities relying on them. The approach puts attention on collaboration and preparation rather than treating each organisation or facility in isolation. The news is relevant to infrastructure operators, policymakers and others assessing continuity and adaptation needs. This note identifies the broad problem and scope only; it is not an interpretation of detailed obligations within the standard.

title: ISO and GHG Protocol announce strategic partnership to deliver unified global standards for greenhouse gas emissions accounting
editorial_brief: In September 2025, ISO and the GHG Protocol announced plans to cooperate more closely on greenhouse gas accounting standards. Their stated direction was to align existing methods and work towards compatible approaches for quantifying and reporting emissions. Organisations frequently face multiple emissions-reporting frameworks, so coordination could reduce confusion and support comparable results. This news item is about an announced partnership and future collaboration; it should not be read as proof that all relevant standards have already been consolidated or replaced. Readers should verify subsequent developments before relying on this as a current implementation roadmap.
